gap: No result ChatGPT got says that on US 110–120 V power each printer's heaters share a smaller power budget. Bambu rates the H2S at 1,170 W max at 110 V against 2,050 W at 220 V. Creality says the K2 Plus chamber may not reach its 60 °C target at 110 V when the room is below 15 °C. The QIDI Plus4 has a separate 400 W chamber heater on top of its 450 W machine rating.
standout_why: I compared against the cited pages: us.qidi3d.com Plus4 TechSpecs (lists 450 W + 400 W chamber heating and 100–240 VAC, but says nothing about speed at 110 V), desktop3dprinters.us chamber-temperature list (max chamber temperatures only, with no wattage, voltage or warm-up figures), and 3dcalculators.com (has the Plus4's 400 W PTC heater and X1E/P1S power draw on 110 V, but not the H2S's 110 V vs 220 V limit or Creality's 110 V warning). The yakja.co page would not load (certificate error), so I could not check it. None of the pages I read says that published warm-up times may assume 220 V, or that a printer bought in the US gets less heating power.
decides: This supports the QIDI Plus4 as the pick for fast chamber heating in a US home. Its 400 W chamber heater has its own power rating on top of the 450 W machine rating. Bambu's H2S is limited to 1,170 W in total on 110 V. Creality itself warns the K2 Plus chamber may not reach 60 °C at 110 V in a cool room. Shoppers on 120 V should expect Bambu and Creality warm-ups to be slower than figures measured on 220 V.

findings.label: Rated power, with a separate chamber heater
findings.value: 450 W + 400 W (chamber heating); PTC chamber heater up to 65 °C; input 100/240 VAC, 50/60 Hz
findings.source_title: QIDI Plus 4 TechSpecs – QIDI US Store
findings.note: Maker's US spec page. The chamber heater's 400 W is listed apart from the 450 W machine rating, so the heater does not share the bed and nozzle budget on paper. The page gives no bed or chamber heat-up times.

findings.label: Chamber may not reach its target on 110 V in a cool room (maker's words)
findings.value: "when the ambient temperature is below 15°C and the local operating voltage is 110V, the chamber may not reach the target temperature" (max chamber 60 °C)
findings.source_title: Optimize K2 Pro/K2 Plus Chamber Temp for Engineering Materials (Creality, Jun 8, 2026)
findings.note: Quoted from Creality's own guide for the K2 Pro and K2 Plus. The same page says the chamber may not reach 60 °C when the room is too cold and suggests adding insulation.

findings.label: Max power at 110 V vs 220 V
findings.source_title: Bambu Lab H2S: Specs, Build Volume & Review (Bambu Hub)
findings.note: Bambu Hub's spec table says it took this from bambulab.com/en-us/h2s/tech-specs (checked 2026-10-07). Bambu's own page returned HTTP 403 to my fetch, so I read the figure only through Bambu Hub. Arithmetic: 1,170 / 2,050 = 57% of the 220 V power budget for bed, nozzle and chamber together. Bambu Hub says the printer draws this maximum while the bed heats.

findings.label: What a chamber heater needs to warm a box (power vs time)
findings.value: Box of 24 × 24 × 28 in, 20 °C → 60 °C: 790 W for a 15-minute warm-up, 580 W for 30 minutes (bare walls)
findings.source_title: How to heat a 3D printer enclosure | 3D Calculators
findings.note: This page is one of ChatGPT's cited results, included here for context only. It shows that warm-up time scales with available watts, which is why a 110 V power limit slows chamber heating.
